messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure is due to a bug in the ClassUtils.getShortClassName method when it is called with array classes. The bug report states that a semicolon is appended to the class name for arrays, for example "String;" instead of "String" or "String[]".

Looking at the available code snippets:
- getShortClassName(Class<?>) just calls getShortClassName(String) with the class name.
- getShortClassName(String) tries to handle array encoding (lines 192-194) but has no actual code there; it just has a placeholder comment "// Handle array encoding" with no implemented logic.
- The rest of getShortClassName(String) just extracts the simple class name by taking the substring after the last '.', handles inner classes, and returns the result.

The presence of the comment about handling array encoding but no implementation indicates a missing feature: the method does not decode the internal array class naming conventions like "[Ljava.lang.String;" which is how Java represents an array of Strings as a class name. Without this decoding, the raw class name "[Ljava.lang.String;" is processed directly, and the resultant output appends the semicolon (the extra character in the internal array name format) to the visible class name string.

The test fails because getShortClassName(String[].class) eventually calls getShortClassName("[Ljava.lang.String;"), and since the method does not strip out the array encoding or remove the trailing semicolon, the output is "String;" instead of the expected "String[]".

Thus, the root cause is missing logic in getShortClassName(String) to parse and properly decode array class names, removing or translating the internal encoding characters like '[', 'L', and ';' into a readable array syntax like "String[]" or "int[]" before extracting the short class name.

Recent bug reports do not reference array class name handling, so they are not relevant here.

Recommendation: add code to getShortClassName(String) to detect array encoding and strip it correctly before extracting the name.

Next, I will fetch the full getShortClassName method to see the exact place and code around the array handling for detailed suggestions.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug occurs in the method org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String). This method is used by getShortClassName(Class<?>) and getShortClassName(Object, String) which make it the core implementation.

From the code, the method currently does these steps:
- Returns empty string if input is null or empty
- Has a comment "Handle array encoding" but does not implement any logic on lines 192-194 to do so
- Finds the last package separator '.' and uses substring to extract the short class name after that
- Handles inner class separator replacement
- Returns the name

The problem arises because Java internal names for arrays are encoded using the format like "[Ljava.lang.String;". When passed directly here, lastIndexOf('.') returns a position on the fully qualified type inside the array encoding (like "java.lang.String" inside), and substring extracts the tail part including the trailing semicolon (e.g., "String;") without any decoding or cleanup.

Since there is no code to decode or clean this array encoding format—despite the comment hinting intention—the function returns the malformed short name for array classes, causing the semicolon suffix.

The current bug report and failing test align perfectly with this finding:
- The test calls getShortClassName(String[].class) which leads to getShortClassName("[Ljava.lang.String;")
- The method extracts "String;" incorrectly instead of converting the array notation to "String[]" or similar
- The bug report mentions unexpected semicolon appended to the output

The root cause is the missing implementation to decode and strip the internal array class name format in the getShortClassName(String) method. The logic should remove or translate the leading '[' characters denoting dimensionality, the 'L' prefix for object types, and trailing semicolon, so the method returns a clean and human-readable class name for arrays.

Recent issue reports do not indicate any related fixes or code relevant to array encoding and can be safely ignored for this bug.

In summary, the method getShortClassName(String) currently lacks the necessary logic to handle Java internal array type names correctly, resulting in erroneous semicolon suffixes in output for array classes, explaining the test failure and bug description. Adding array processing logic here will fix the issue.
